_comment: Scoped seccomp profile for quarry-edge so Chromium keeps its OWN sandbox inside the container. Chromium builds its sandbox from unprivileged user and PID namespaces (clone/unshare with CLONE_NEWUSER/CLONE_NEWPID) and a setuid-free namespace sandbox; Docker's DEFAULT profile blocks that, which is why the dev compose used to run Chromium with --no-sandbox. This profile is allow-by-default plus an explicit deny-list of escape/escalation syscalls (derived from apps/Model Plane/deploy/seccomp-bwrap.json), strictly safer than seccomp=unconfined and than --no-sandbox. clone, clone3, unshare and setns are intentionally NOT in the deny-list. Wire via: security_opt: [ seccomp=./seccomp-chromium.json ] on quarry-edge ONLY (path relative to the compose file).

syscalls.comment: Block container-escape / host-compromise / kernel-module / time / keyring primitives. clone, clone3, unshare and setns are intentionally NOT here so Chromium can build its namespace sandbox.
